content.user_title: Design Email Preference and Frequency Controls
content.value_statement: Subscribers leave when cadence and topic choices feel rigid. This skill designs preference centers and opt-down ladders that reduce opt-outs while preserving consent.
actual_capabilities: Defines topic groups, cadence tiers, channel toggles, and save behavior for preference pages.
Designs opt-down ladders that offer reduced frequency, topic selection, pause, and full unsubscribe.
Maps each preference choice to an ESP suppression or frequency rule.
Produces a SEND N sub-item note for preference-center and frequency options.
Creates a handoff summary for sequence design, consent registry, or quality audit workflows.
limitations: Does not compute the full Email Quality Score or rule the N1 unsubscribe veto.
Does not own the canonical consent or suppression record.
Does not build lifecycle flow maps or global send-cap governance.
Needs user-provided topics, cadence context, or an ESP export for measured current-state analysis.

use_cases.title: Reduce newsletter unsubscribes
use_cases.description: Design a preference center that lets subscribers choose topics and lower cadence before leaving.

use_cases.title: Map preferences to ESP rules
use_cases.description: Translate topic toggles, pause options, and cadence tiers into rules the ESP can honor.

use_cases.title: Prepare for SEND audit
use_cases.description: Produce the preference-center sub-item note used by the email quality auditor.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic preference center
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a known audience and topic list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a preference center for our newsletter. Topics are product updates, events, and promotions. Offer weekly, monthly, and pause options.

prompt_templates.title: Design an opt-down ladder
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an opt-down ladder for subscribers who click unsubscribe. Offer reduced cadence, topic selection, a 90-day pause, and full unsubscribe.

prompt_templates.title: Repair a fatigue segment
prompt_templates.prompt: Opt-outs are rising for dormant buyers. Design topic and cadence choices, then map each choice to suppression or frequency rules.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an audit handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this preference-center plan and produce the SEND N sub-item note, open loops, and next-skill handoff summary.

output_examples.input: A retail list sends weekly promotions and wants fewer hard unsubscribes.
output: Preference fields include promotions, new arrivals, events, and partner offers.
The ladder offers monthly cadence, topic-only mail, a 90-day pause, then full unsubscribe.
Each choice maps to an ESP suppression, cap, or pause-until rule.

output_examples.input: A B2B newsletter needs topic controls before a SEND audit.
output: The plan separates product updates, education, webinars, and company news.
The SEND N note is Partial until pause behavior and consent-registry recording are confirmed.
Open loops list missing ESP export and cadence-tier enforcement evidence.

output_examples.input: A dormant segment needs a lighter cadence before sunset suppression.
output: The ladder starts with monthly cadence, then topic-only mail, then a 120-day pause.
The sunset terminus triggers after the pause if no engagement returns.
The handoff routes cadence governance to the sequence designer.

best_practices: Keep full unsubscribe reachable in one click after presenting softer options.
Offer only cadence tiers and topic choices that the ESP can enforce reliably.
Record each topic, cadence, and pause choice as an explicit suppression or frequency rule.
anti_patterns: Hiding unsubscribe behind required preference questions or extra confirmation steps.
Offering vague topic groups that cannot map to real email streams.
Creating monthly or pause options without operational rules that enforce them.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a preference-center field spec, an opt-down ladder, rule mappings, and a SEND N sub-item note.

faq.question: Does it replace consent management?
faq.answer: No. It designs the mapping, but the consent registry remains the canonical record.

faq.question: Can it work without an ESP export?
faq.answer: Yes. It can design from stated topics and cadence tiers, then mark current-state evidence as unavailable.

faq.question: Does it compute the Email Quality Score?
faq.answer: No. It provides a sub-item note for the email quality auditor to use later.

faq.question: How does it reduce unsubscribes?
faq.answer: It gives subscribers lower cadence, fewer topics, or a pause before they choose a full opt-out.

faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible skill hosts.
